findings.claim: Attributes on T are ignored when there is no surrogate. CreateContractlessMembers serializes every public read-write member by name and never reads [DataContract]/[DataMember]/[IgnoreDataMember] or [MessagePackObject]/[Key]/[IgnoreMember]. Example: a Project A type `[DataContract] class MyType { [DataMember(Order=0)] public int A {get;set;} [IgnoreDataMember] public string Secret {get;set;} public string Unmarked {get;set;} }`. The generated formatter writes Secret and Unmarked under string keys. This breaks the acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured', and members the type author excluded leak onto the wire.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterHonoursTypeAttributesTests.DataContractAttributesOnReferencedTypeAreHonoured. It compiles Project A with [DataContract]/[IgnoreDataMember] to a metadata reference, runs MessagePackGenerator on Project B with [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter], and asserts the generated source does not mention 'Secret' or 'Unmarked'. On head it fails.

findings.claim: Surrogate mode treats every instance field and property of the surrogate as part of the contract, including private fields and non-public or get-only helpers. Any such member without [Key] or [IgnoreMember] fails with MsgPack004 and no formatter is generated. Example: a surrogate with `private int _cache;` or `internal string Note {get;set;}`. Normal [MessagePackObject] validation only requires keys on public members (L5), and the attribute docs only constrain members that carry [Key].

receipt_plan.detail: Generator test: surrogate `class S { [Key(0)] public int A {get;set;} private int _helper; }` with T having public int A. Expect a formatter to be generated and no MsgPack004. On head the generator emits MsgPack004 on _helper and produces no formatter.

findings.claim: GetInstanceMembers dedupes by name before the accessibility and read-write filter, so a more-derived member that fails IsPublicReadWrite hides a valid base member. The property is then silently dropped from the contractless contract. Examples: `class Base { public virtual int X {get;set;} } class Derived : Base { public override int X { get => base.X; } }` (the override symbol has SetMethod == null), or a derived `private new int X;` hiding a public base X.

receipt_plan.detail: Generator test with the Base/Derived get-only-override shape above and `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<Derived>`. Assert the generated formatter serializes X. On head X is missing.

findings.claim: The collector checks only that the formatter class itself is partial, not that its containing types are. The templates emit the formatter inside EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces(Info.Formatter). A formatter nested in a non-partial class (`class Outer { [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] public partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<T> {} }`) would therefore get generated code that redeclares Outer, giving CS0260 or a duplicate type, instead of a MsgPack019 diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: IsPartial (GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:291-297) inspects only formatter.DeclaringSyntaxReferences and never ContainingType. FormatterTemplate.tt line 14 wraps output in EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces for Info.Formatter. Confirm by compiling the generated output for the nested case.
